text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike in driver resets detected from serving-prod-gpu-pool (us-west-2). 18 resets in last 10m across 6 nodes. Severity: P1 if customer impact > 5% errors. Paging on-call.

mike_oncall: on it. mounting a bridge, grabbing logs now. Which pool exactly?

raj_infra: hitting serving-prod-gpu-pool-{a..f} per telemetry. kernel shows repeated nv-host reset sequence and Xid 31-like messages but not identical. Looks like correctable ECC + driver oops pattern. grabbing dmesg tail now:  

```
[ 4278.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=4321, Graphics Reset
[ 4278.123467] kernel: nv-host: gpu reset called
[ 4278.124001] device-mapper: reload failed on /dev/nvme0n1p3
[ 4279.000873] gpu0: ECC: corrected 1 bits at 0x7f1a23
[ 4279.001002] nv_peer_mem: peer memory callback failed
```

jen_devops: also seeing container crashes in the runtime pods on those nodes, crashloop backoffs. kubelet reports OOMKill on some model containers just prior to driver reset.

alex_support: any customer-facing errors yet? I have two customers who pinged monitoring: latency spikes and 5xxs for inference calls to hosted endpoints. Not widespread but noisy.

mike_oncall: marking as paging P1 until impact determined. @alex_support please gather request IDs or endpoints. I'll coordinate mitigations.

alex_support: sent request ids to #customer-bridges. Top affected endpoints: /v1/generate/large-model-prod and /v1/chat/streamer. Error pattern: 502 gateway + connection reset.

raj_infra: quick triage plan: 1) isolate nodes with highest reset rate, 2) cordon+drain non-critical pods, 3) fall back to CPU-variant routing for affected endpoints via traffic-policy, 4) collect full kernel+driver logs and nvstack dumps, 5) consider rolling a driver rollback if we see correlation with 535.54 driver.

tess_sre: agree. I'll take node isolation/evac. Starting cordon on serving-prod-gpu-pool-c right now.

jen_devops: command run: 
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-c && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-c --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

jen_devops: pods are draining. Autoscaler triggered to spin up fallback CPU instances.

mike_oncall: enabling traffic-policy fallback for endpoints listed by @alex_support. Patch applied to route 20% to cpu-variant, 80% to remaining healthy gpus.

alex_support: customers notified via status page draft (prelim): "We're investigating elevated error rates for some inference requests in US-WEST. Mitigations in progress; some traffic redirected. More updates in 30m." Approving publish.

raj_infra: noticed ECC correctable counts rising on nodes before resets. Might be a thermal/voltage transient causing memory correctables that later trigger driver watchdog. Check hwmon temps: 
```
cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp
# gpu temps: 85C on node-f, 88C on node-c
```

jen_devops: infra note: node-f has a fan spindown warning in IPMI logs just before the first resets. Might be flaky BMC firmware.

mike_oncall: ok immediate actions: 1) keep affected nodes cordoned and drained, 2) place them in maintenance (no scheduling), 3) boot a spare host and migrate workloads, 4) enable driver watchdog backoff config to avoid cascade. Who can run a driver rollback test?

raj_infra: I can test driver rollback on a single spare. Will provision spare, install stable driver 540.xx there and run load tests for 30m. If stable, plan to roll 1 node at a time.

alex_support: customers on the bridge asking about data loss — none reported, only transient failures. Confirming logs: no persisted request loss; retries succeed. Communicating that to customers now.

jen_devops: running nvstack dump for node-c -> uploaded to /artifacts/2629991234/node-c-nvstack.log

mike_oncall: starting incident bridge: https://meet.company/bridges/2629991234 (bridge pinned). All core responders join.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2629991234. Severity: P1 (proactive) — owner: mike_oncall. Slack thread pinned to channel.

tess_sre: quick heuristic: throttle batch sizes on the large-model-prod route to reduce resident memory. Patch env var for runtime pods: MAX_BATCH=4 -> applied on canary nodes.

raj_infra: load test on spare with 540 driver completed 30m with no resets. baseline memory and ECC counts stable. I recommend rolling nodes to 540 driver as interim while we dig into BMC/thermal faults.

mike_oncall: approved. Start rolling driver downgrade on cordoned nodes, 1 at a time, confirm health for 15m post-roll, then uncordon.

jen_devops: rolling: node-c -> done, post-checks good. node-f -> in progress.

alex_support: status update posted to status page. Customers on bridge acknowledged the mitigation. They want ETA for full resolution, giving provisional 3h for node roll + post-verification.

mike_oncall: customer impact summary for handoff: ~2 customers saw ~5-7% error increase over 12m window; a handful of self-serve customers had latency spikes up to 2-3x. No data loss. Fallback routing reduced errors by half.

tess_sre: operational actions for next shift: 1) complete driver rollback on remaining impacted nodes, 2) replace/inspect BMC on node-f, 3) add thermal backoff in device plugin to avoid aggressive clocks under high temp, 4) add alert to correlate ECC correctable rate with resets.

raj_infra: note for postmortem: collect firmware versions (BMC, BIOS), driver version history, ECC counts trend, nv-host stack traces, and kubelet OOM logs.

mike_oncall: handing off to night shift at 2629991402. Summary below.

--- HANDOFF SUMMARY ---
Incident id: INC-2629991234
Start: 2629991234
Handoff: 2629991402
Owner: mike_oncall -> oncall-night
Impact: transient 5xx and latency spikes for a subset of hosted inference endpoints (two customers elevated), reduced after partial fallback and node isolation.
Mitigation taken: cordon+drain 3 nodes, route fallback to cpu-variant (20% then adjusted), throttle batch sizes on canary, rolling driver rollback to stable 540.xx, live nvstack dumps collected, bridge created.
Next steps: finish driver roll on remaining nodes, replace/inspect BMC on node-f, correlate ECC counts -> decide on hardware replacement if correctables persist, write postmortem within 72h.
Contacts: raj_infra, tess_sre, alex_support.

mike_oncall: leaving notes in pagerduty. All responders acknowledge?

raj_infra: ack.

tess_sre: ack.

alex_support: ack.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2629991234 moved to monitoring state.
